Where the first syllable needed to be long, the tragedians said ἀμός [my], on which see above p. 23.
speak – having cast off my shame
Schol. exp. ἐμπαισάσαις [having rushed upon]. Similar is πρόσπαιος [sudden] v. 338.

where M has καὶ κρυπτά γ᾽ ἤρας ταῦτα παλλαγμάτων [and these hidden things of Hera's embraces]. Correctly Hermannus: "the scholiast's note αἱ περιπλοκαί [the embraces] and the corrupt Hesychius ἐμπαλεύγματα: αἱ ἐμπλοκαί [entanglements] could have shown that what I have written is what should be written. He said 'embrace': for ἐμπαλάσσεσθαι [to be entangled] means 'to be involved', as in Herodotus 7, 85 and Thucydides 7, 84 and others."
